v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first because impl-2 has one real correctness bug. Both architectures are almost the same and close to ideal: an atomic conditional update in markAsPaid with an afterCommit dispatch, the global 'warehouse' RateLimited middleware at 5 per second, WithoutOverlapping, retryUntil with Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout attributes, an Idempotency-Key header, a capped Retry-After release on 429, a fail() on 422, and an atomic claim on shipment_notified_at so the email goes out once. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 25 tests, impl-1: 22).

The bug: impl-2's failed() always marks the order Failed. If the shipment was created but the mail keeps failing until retries run out, the order goes from Sent to Failed while it still has a shipment reference. That misleads ops about a shipment that exists and risks a duplicate shipment if they redo it by hand. My probe confirmed it. impl-1 guards failed() with whereNull('shipment_reference') and also re-checks that the order is paid. My second probe showed impl-2 calls the warehouse for an unpaid order if the job is dispatched directly; this is minor because only markAsPaid dispatches it.

In impl-2's favour: it has the richer test suite (real mail transport failure, 422 run end-to-end, failure-reason dataset, rate limit checked by running it out) and nicer model intent methods. impl-1's tests are weaker in places (the after-commit test never checks afterCommit; the 422 test calls failed() by hand), but its own tests cover the Sent-protection case.

Both failed my MaxAttemptsExceeded probe with 'Undefined array key "job"'. That was a mistake in how I built the probe, not a bug in either implementation, so I ignored it.

On balance, the Sent-to-Failed overwrite goes directly against the task's requirements to avoid duplicate shipments and give ops an accurate failure status, so impl-1 ranks first.
